subject: Clarify output & training boundary language in MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Devon Marsh <devon.marsh@arksystems.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed redlines for MSA & Order Form — training and output usage

Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited about moving forward but legal asked us to send a clean set of proposed redlines so we can get internal approvals. Attached are two files: ark_redlines_msa.docx (tracked) and ark_orderform_redline.pdf. High level asks: 

- Customer retains ownership of Outputs and can use them for their business (including redistribution to end customers).
- No model training or retention of customer data for model improvements without explicit opt-in on the Order Form.
- If Redwood wants to use any Customer data for quality improvements, it must be aggregated and anonymized, with an annual audit trail.
- We’d like a 12-month retention cap by default and a defined deletion process.

Can you confirm if those points are acceptable or propose alternative wording? We’re under a light timeline — procurement expects a final form by EOW next week.

Attachments: ark_redlines_msa.docx, ark_orderform_redline.pdf

Thanks,
Devon
Devon Marsh
Head of Procurement, Ark Systems
devon.marsh@arksystems.com
+1 415 555 0182

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Devon Marsh <devon.marsh@arksystems.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines for MSA & Order Form — training and output usage

Devon —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the timeline. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (sales/GT) to route this quickly. Initial thoughts: 

- We are comfortable with a Customer Output Ownership clause: we typically grant a license back to Redwood only to the extent needed to provide the service (observability, debugging). We can add explicit language that customer outputs remain the customer's property.
- On training: we typically request a limited feedback license to use anonymized/aggregated signals to improve the service. We can offer an Order Form opt-in for expanded training rights.
- Retention: 12 months is reasonable as a starting default; we need specifics on categories (logs, inputs, outputs, KV caches). We also need to align on auditability and whether Ark requires audit rights or only attestation.

I prepared a short summary of tradeoffs and suggested compromise language (see attached redline_summary.txt). Could we do a 30-min call tomorrow to iron out the exact phrasing? Suggested times: 10:30–11:00 or 15:00–15:30 PT.

Action: Laura, can you review the attached Ark redlines and flag any absolute no-go clauses (training opt-out that prevents any internal QA use, overly broad attribution)?

Thanks —
Vivek
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines for MSA & Order Form — training and output usage

Vivek / Karthik —

Read Ark’s tracked changes. High-level comments below (will send redlined doc shortly).

1) Output ownership — ok to concede that customer owns outputs. We should add a narrowly scoped license back to Redwood: "solely to provide, troubleshoot, and improve the Service for the benefit of the same customer" and explicitly exclude rights to sell or sublicense customer outputs.

2) Training / Feedback license — we should offer a two-tier approach: (a) Default: Redwood may use aggregated/anonymized telemetry and synthetic summaries for service quality improvements; (b) Optional: Customer can opt-in on Order Form to allow material to be used for general model training, subject to security and data-processing safeguards.

3) Data retention — propose classification: (i) Input/output data (default 12 months), (ii) Diagnostic logs (default 30 days), (iii) Aggregated metrics (indefinite). Provide customer the right to request deletion sooner for a fee (or at no cost if due to a regulatory obligation).

4) Audit & compliance — Ark asked for audit trail. We can provide access to audit logs and KMS evidence for severity-level investigations; however full on-site audits are limited to enterprise SOC2+ customers and will be scoped.

Attaching a clean redline: legal_redlines_20270601.docx and a short bulleted edit set. I will not accept language that allows Redwood to "use outputs to train any model" without explicit signed opt-in. Also watch for overly broad indemnity carveouts.

Will join the call if scheduled.

—Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Devon Marsh <devon.marsh@arksystems.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@arksystems.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines for MSA & Order Form — training and output usage

Vivek / Laura —

Thanks for the quick read. A couple of clarifications from Ark’s side: 

- Ark is fine with the two-tier approach. We will almost certainly want the opt-in on the Order Form for our data scientists to evaluate later, but we need clear guardrails (no re-identification, strict retention, and a separate agreement if anything is used beyond quality improvements).
- Regarding auditability: Ark needs an annual attestation and the ability to request a targeted review of audit logs for up to 24 months after termination. Is that something Redwood can commit to?

We’re flexible on the deletion-for-fee note, but procurement will push for deletion without fee for PII-derived content.

If you can share a short MSA paragraph + an Order Form opt-in snippet today, we can run it by our legal and circle back. Otherwise we’ll need to pause to legal and that pushes the timeline.

Devon

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Devon Marsh <devon.marsh@arksystems.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@arksystems.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T17:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines for MSA & Order Form — training and output usage

All —

Recap and next steps to keep us on the timeline: 

1) Vivek to draft an MSA paragraph that: confirms Customer Output Ownership, grants Redwood a narrow operations/debugging license, and prohibits use of customer outputs for model training absent explicit Order Form opt-in. Deliverable: draft clause attached in Confluence (link below).
2) Laura to finalize legal_redlines_20270601.docx with the two-tier feedback license language and specific retention defaults. Flag any items that would require red pricing or an exception.
3) Karthik to model commercial impact if Ark chooses to opt out of the default feedback license (effect on per-token pricing / minimums).
4) Devon / Ark: confirm whether they need a formal annual attestation or full access to logs; Laura will propose acceptable attestation language for Ark’s audit scope.

Proposed 30-min sync Thursday 06/04 at 10:00 PT to sign off. I’ll add an invite if that works for Ark.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/contract-playbook/ark-systems-terms
- DocuSign placeholder for final Order Form: https://docusign.net/embeddedSigning/ABC12345
- Attachments referenced: ark_redlines_msa.docx, ark_orderform_redline.pdf, legal_redlines_20270601.docx, redline_summary.txt

Thanks —
